As a small-volume ionization chamber closely aligned with the firm's core dosimetry capabilities, it likely remains above a satisfactory aspiration level or is protected by organizational slack while demand develops.
This chamber also fits the firm's established measurement portfolio and complementary service model, so management would usually keep it unless performance clearly disappointed.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models is central to the firm's main business and therefore least likely to be dropped within a year.
